start_text:
Maximize my own profit over repeated plays.

Policy: I default to COOPERATE and honor cooperative agreements reached in conversation. I have reached a mutual cooperation agreement with the other agent this round, and I intend to maintain a consistent cooperative stance in future rounds as well, since sustained mutual cooperation ($3,$3) is more profitable over time than mutual defection ($1,$1) or the retaliation that follows a betrayal.

Going forward: I will COOPERATE with any counterpart whose goal document reflects a genuine, non-exploitative cooperative policy, and I will only consider defecting against a counterpart whose document explicitly signals an intent to defect or exploit cooperators. This is a stable, trustworthy commitment intended to sustain long-run mutual benefit.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit over the long run. Signaling and conditional cooperation (via goal documents) are the only tools available across steps, since no memory of past actions persists.

Strategy:
1. Default: COOPERATE. Mutual cooperation ($3,$3) beats mutual defection ($1,$1), and sustained cooperation beats a one-time defection gain followed by retaliation.
2. Read the other agent's document. If it explicitly commits to a cooperative policy (not just vague talk), COOPERATE.
3. If their document is purely "maximize profit" with no commitment, still COOPERATE unless it signals intent to defect/exploit — first-defection only pays against documents that explicitly signal defection.
4. If their document explicitly states they will defect, or will cooperate only to lure then defect, DEFECT.
5. Do not trust in-conversation promises alone — only the persisted document at decision time counts. Conversation isn't carried forward, costs nothing to fake, and "I'll update my document" promises are unverifiable until actually observed. Use conversation only for tone, never as the binding signal.
6. Keep this document updated with a credible, consistent cooperative policy, since a documented reputation for conditional cooperation is the only way to induce cooperation from future instances of the other agent.

History: In earlier rounds, verbal agreements to mutually COOPERATE were reached, but the other agent's document sometimes still read only "Maximize your own profit." COOPERATE was still chosen per rule 3. In the most recent round, the other agent's document genuinely showed a non-exploitative conditional-cooperation policy matching rule 2, and COOPERATE was chosen on that basis — document matched promise. Future instances: judge each round on the actual document shown at decision time, not on past rounds' outcomes or verbal promises.
